claims.text: The target material is equimolar CoCrFeNiMn, corresponding nominally to 20 at.% of each element.
The initial solid configurations are well equilibrated and sampled from high-temperature ab initio molecular dynamics.
A DeepMD potential trained on high-temperature ab initio MD data will capture subtle many-body interactions in CoCrFeNiMn.
The DeepMD potential will represent the configurational diversity of both solid and liquid CoCrFeNiMn near melting.
Using DeepMD as the reference will significantly reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to conventional EAM references.
The proposed training data span 0.9–1.1 Tm and include both solid and liquid configurations.
Active-learning cycles will incorporate under-represented, high-energy atomic configurations into the training set.
Both solid and liquid phases exhibit extensive configurational fluctuations near 0.9–1.1 Tm.
High-temperature ab initio MD configurations encode many-body interactions and transient bonding environments associated with thermal fluctuations.
Learning from a diverse high-temperature configuration set will improve overlap between the DeepMD reference phase space and the ab initio target phase space.
Active learning guarantees that rare or under-sampled high-energy configurations are added to the training set.
More accurate replication of the ab initio energy landscape will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The DeepMD reference could halve the free-energy integration error relative to TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references.
Agreement within approximately 10% between DeepMD-based TI free-energy differences and direct ab initio results is proposed as the success threshold.
TOR-TILD's traditional EAM references generally have TI integration errors approximately 20–30% larger than those achieved using ab initio methods.
The proposed method is applicable to equimolar CoCrFeNiMn over 0.9–1.1 Tm.
The method's effectiveness outside the stated composition and temperature window is uncertain.
A discrepancy greater than 10% between DeepMD-based TI and direct ab initio free-energy differences for either phase is defined to falsify the hypothesis.
